A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MapDR study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, appendices A–J, and supplementary listings support comparison despite resizing and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original MapDR experiments, including method comparisons, component ablations, lane-type evaluations, repeated-seed results, and zero-shot MLLM evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 2–5, Figure 11, and the supplementary examples.

M1.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix I retain the same VLE-MEE and RuleVLM architectures, encoding components, losses, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MapDR coverage from Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou for rule extraction and rule-lane correspondence. Waymo is added only to the descriptive dataset comparison in Table 1; no Waymo experiment is reported.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the heuristic, ALBEF-BERT, and Qwen-VL text/visual-prompt comparisons. Appendix J and Table 5 retain Qwen-VL Max, Gemini Pro, Claude3 Opus, and GPT-4V.

E3.justification: The 9:1 train/test split, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix J retains the same 180-case zero-shot evaluation and subjective assessment procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the attention/layout/embedding ablations in Table 3, lane-type analysis in Table 4, seed analysis in Figure 11, and MLLM case studies in Figures 15–16. Their relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix I.4 retains five runs with the same listed seeds, threshold sampling, mean precision-recall curve, and standard-deviation reporting. No statistical procedure or uncertainty disclosure is added.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their numerical results; for example, Table 2 reports overall F1 scores of 0.653 for VLE-MEE and 0.642 for RuleVLM in both versions. The plotted distributions, precision-recall curves, and qualitative examples also match.

T1.justification: The bipartite-graph task formulation, metric equations (1)–(7), and Appendix H's worked example are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or revised mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, MapDR dataset contribution, and modular/end-to-end baseline claims. The added code link changes access information.

C2.justification: The interpretations of attention, vector encoding, and spatial-reasoning performance remain unchanged. Appendices F and J retain the same safety concerns and qualifications about subjective evaluation, Chinese prompts/OCR, and visual prompting.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 replaces planned releases on Tianchi/ModelScope and GitHub with specific ModelScope dataset and GitHub code locations. D.3 specifies the maintenance page, and the abstract adds the code link. Implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Waymo to Table 1 and adds the corresponding Waymo Open Dataset reference. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 regroups author affiliations and contact information, shortens several references to supplementary material, and replaces the contents list with a supplementary-material title. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several figures are reduced in size and reflowed; Figure 8 moves from page 8 to page 7, and Figure 4 uses recompressed graphics. Table 1 gains a Waymo row, while supplementary figures and tables shift position without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves resource discoverability through concrete dataset and code locations, replacing v2's planned-release descriptions in Appendix D.2–D.3 and adding a code link to the abstract. This is a limited documentation gain, with unchanged scientific evidence and a modest navigation tradeoff from removing the contents list.
